floor.basis: observed: the full suite is green on 3.8.10 and on every minor from 3.9 to 3.14, each measured on a portable CPython build on one VM and then again on a CI matrix row (T-0034). Nothing in tools/originlib uses syntax newer than 3.8
floor.not_claimed: 3.15 and newer has never been run here, and nothing predicts it will pass. Contiguity from 3.8 to 3.14 is evidence about those minors and nothing more; a floor is supported by the oldest interpreter the suite passes on, and no amount of green rows upgrades it to a claim about the rest of the range

not_exercised.why: no interpreter of 3.15 or newer has been run: neither VM has one, and no CI matrix row requests one
not_exercised.consequence: a defect that appears only from 3.15 onwards would not be caught by any row, and the floor claim is a hope rather than a measurement at that edge

not_exercised.range: any non-CPython implementation, or a non-Linux platform
not_exercised.why: never attempted; every entry above is CPython on Linux x86_64
not_exercised.consequence: the claim is CPython on Linux only

related_defect.note: Solved in T-0033: doctor compares this VM's interpreter and git against this record and reports exercised / NOT exercised / record unreadable / no record. Solved again, in a different place, in T-0034: the record and the CI matrix were not connected, so the suite failed on every interpreter the record had not heard of (F018). tests/test_ci_matrix.py now holds the two to each other in both directions.

note: Machine-readable companion to git-versions.json. It exists because docs/operations/vm-execution.md said plainly that no gate pinned a Python range, and because a mission record once demanded a 3.11+ floor invented from one machine's 3.14.6 (T-0023) - a claim about an interpreter the fleet has never run. Each entry's scope says how much of the suite that version has actually run, because a version that ran an older suite is not evidence about the current one, and each entry's where says which machine or runner it ran on, because one record now covers two environments per minor version. The matrix itself lives in .github/workflows/ci.yml and is not duplicated here: a second copy of the row list would be a second thing to keep in step.
